findings.observation: Hero and top show the five-knob arrangement expected by the contract: one left control, three rear-center controls and one right control, with the rear macro strip, two left-side macro keys and the wide spacebar all present. The 284:92 product proportion remains coherent. The Full HD proof is 16:9 while the primary owner photo is 2048x1534 (about 4:3), so the surrounding composition and apparent perspective are not a camera-matched reproduction; this is a framing/aspect delta rather than a gross layout divergence.
findings.action: No correction is required for the declared layout criterion. A later marketing-fidelity pass could match the owner photo camera and crop more closely without changing world-space layout.

findings.observation: Rounded charcoal key faces, short visible skirts and white legends are consistent and readable at Full HD. The close-up shows no floating lettering or broken key family. Relative to the owner references, the legend set is simplified: several secondary symbols, multi-line labels and small board markings are omitted or represented by generic dots/single glyphs, so textual fidelity remains below the source artwork even though the modeled key-form criterion passes.
findings.action: No geometry correction is required. If closer visual identity is needed, transcribe and place the exact owner-approved legend/secondary-mark artwork in a later presentation revision.

findings.observation: The knob close-up shows a recessed top indicator channel as geometry, not a painted line. The cylindrical side now reads smooth at Full HD; the earlier vertical faceting/banding is no longer visible. The small sharp opening where the channel exits the beveled rim is consistent with the modeled channel intersecting that rim and does not by itself indicate a surface-faceting defect.
findings.action: No visual correction is required for the declared slot/surface criterion. Retain the sharp channel boundary unless a later owner reference establishes a different edge treatment.

findings.observation: Hero and exploded views clearly separate the dark plate, PCB, translucent acrylic layer and silver lower body. Real RGB emitters and a blue-purple-pink/orange perimeter response are visible, especially in the exploded view. Compared with the owner photo and 360 design guide, the assembled hero is more restrained: the acrylic glow is paler and less saturated, with less cyan/orange edge emphasis and less bloom. The illumination delta is visual/material-lighting fidelity, not a missing layer.
findings.action: The declared layered-body/RGB criterion passes. If closer owner-reference presentation is desired, tune emission, diffuser response and exposure in a later visual-polish pass without changing mechanical geometry.

findings.observation: The underside is fully framed and readable in the Full HD proof, with a silver lower plate and four separate dark feet. No gross crop or missing foot is visible. The secondary 360 illustration includes a centered product/marking panel that is absent here; omitting it avoids inventing certification artwork but remains a visible fidelity delta relative to that owner design guide.
findings.action: No correction is required for the declared underside criterion. Add only owner-verified underside artwork later if that branding detail is required; do not infer certification marks.

findings.observation: All three declared revision-B interface additions are directly inspectable: the key close-up exposes a true cross-shaped receiver, the spacebar underside shows two separate integral guide pins flanking the central receiver, and the knob underside exposes the stepped D-shaped receiver. None is substituted by a flat relief or hidden by framing. These are prototype design features and are not evidence that the hidden geometry of the owner photo used these exact interfaces.
findings.action: No visual correction is required for the declared modeled-interface criterion. Keep physical fit/retention conclusions tied to the separate digital-fit evidence and bench testing.

findings.observation: The encoder-mount proof shows the D shaft, mounting hardware, carrier/board structure and support posts as a connected assembly. The USB close-up shows the generic USB-C shell seated through the side opening with supporting board/chassis geometry visible behind it; it is not floating or visually disconnected. The evidence supports inspectability of the declared prototype hardware only, not electrical footprint, adhesive/bond strength, thread preload, thermal behavior or vendor interchangeability.
findings.action: No visual correction is required for the declared support-hardware criterion. Preserve the existing qualification limits for physical and electrical claims.
